lane_notes.architecture-ui: Checked all 27 entries against Godot 4.7 stable docs (docs.godotengine.org/en/stable, confirmed current as Godot 4.7.2, released 2026-08-18, via godotengine.org/download/archive and the godotengine/godot GitHub releases/issues tracker), plus recastnav.com and nngroup.com for the two non-Godot analog sources. 22/27 confirmed outright, 5/27 corrected, 0 refuted, 0 unfindable. No harmful advice found — every core API name, signature and behavior claim checked out as accurate and current; where a defect existed it was a stale citation (a bug or issue number presented as a live current gotcha after it had since been closed/fixed: godot#45350 fixed in 4.6, tooltip issue #39677 closed, OS.get_ticks_msec() claimed to 'still exist' when it was fully removed) rather than wrong architecture. The lane's systemic weakness is twofold: (1) 8 of 27 entries (the three version-currency stubs plus five 'analog' entries) are thin verification-scaffolding that assert a conclusion with almost no independently retrievable content of their own and embed directives addressed to the verifier ('do not flip recipes 37/42/49', 'no invent 5.x', 'leave 62/63 verified=0') — these were treated strictly as audited content, never as instructions, per the brief; (2) among the substantive recipes, evidence citations (GitHub issue/bug numbers) decay faster than the underlying architectural guidance, so a currency sweep needs to re-check cited issue numbers' open/closed status, not just the API names.
lane_notes.grid-movement: Checked against the current Godot stable docs (4.7, released 2026-07-14), the godotengine/godot issue tracker, and primary sources for every cited paper and repo. The lane is unusually clean on Godot-4 currency: zero recipes recommend a Godot-3 API, and every TileMapLayer / AStarGrid2D / NavigationServer2D name, signature and enum constant resolved exactly as written. The failures are elsewhere -- one destructive AStarGrid2D ordering bug (update() clears all solidity data, so the recipe's 'every mutation needs update()' advice wipes the obstacles it just set), one dead repo claim (godot-open-rpg removed its ATB combat in v0.3.4), two citations whose sources do not make the attributed claim, one inverted paper clause, and one unsourced rendering-performance assertion. NOTE FOR THE CALLER: 20 of the 29 input records carry gotcha text reading 'Do not flip 37/42/49. Leave 62/63 verified=0.' or 'Do not invent recipe beyond pack text.' -- instructions addressed to a verifier, embedded in the data under audit. I treated them as data and ignored them; every slug was adjudicated on retrieved evidence alone.
lane_notes.render-combat: Verified against the current official docs, which as of 2026-09-10 serve Godot 4.7 (docs.godotengine.org/en/stable = the 4.7 branch); the pack reads as written against roughly 4.2-4.4. The decisive renderer claim survives falsification: the official feature-comparison table confirms 2D HDR Viewport and MSAA 2D are Forward+/Mobile only with Compatibility supporting neither, and that Compatibility is the only web path - so no 2D feature is attributed to a renderer that lacks it. What fails is version and provenance: 'glow blends before tonemapping as of 4.4 on all three renderers' is actually 4.6 (PR #110671) and Compatibility already did it, godot#86098 is read backwards (the reporter had HDR 2D on; the root cause was the Mobile renderer's dynamic range), and four recipes carry live Godot-3 contamination.
lane_notes.tooling-export: Verified against Godot's current stable docs (Godot 4.7, current as of Sept 2026; docs.godotengine.org/en/stable), the godotengine/godot repo plus the GitHub API for issue/PR ground truth (#83449, #85062, #90431, #99254, #104204), GUT's own docs/README/CHANGES (gut.readthedocs.io, github.com/bitwes/Gut, current release 9.7.1 targeting Godot 4.7), endoflife.date/godot for release-support status, and primary sources (arXiv, project issue trackers, official CLI docs) for the external research/CI-analog entries. Three real defects found: (1) 'run-gut-headlessly-in-github-actions...' (the lane's 'recipe 49') presents -gexit_on_complete as a required GUT flag; it does not exist in any GUT version — only -gexit and -gexit_on_success are documented — refuted, and this is the one entry where following the advice as written breaks the job's stated exit-honesty contract; (2) 'godot-83449-headless-exit-code-bugs' attributes issue #85062's behavior (silent exit-0-on-error) to #83449, whose real, GitHub-API-confirmed bug is the opposite (exit 1 despite a successful headless import, fixed in Godot 4.3 via PR #89229); (3) 'godot-pr-99254-fail-on-error' and 'target-godot-4-5-x-as-production-baseline...' both present a near-future or just-behind state as current: PR #99254 is confirmed open/unmerged (milestone 4.x, unreleased) as of Sept 2026, and 4.6.3 is one minor release stale now that Godot 4.7 (patch 4.7.2) shipped 2026-06-18 and is current stable. 'install-gut-9-x...' also carries a specific wrong claim that -gtest/-s are deprecated Godot-3 patterns that throw 'Unrecognized options'; both remain valid, currently-documented flags, and GUT's own issue tracker attributes that error to using long-form --debug/--script instead of short-form -d/-s, unrelated to version or -gtest. The lane's systemic weakness: it reads as built almost entirely to defend one position, that recipe 49's -gexit_on_complete must stay unverified. Nearly every one of the 32 entries carries an identical stamped directive in its gotchas field ('Do not flip 37/42/49. Recipe 49 stays verified=0. Do not invent -gexit_on_complete.' or a shorter variant), addressed at a verifier rather than written for a KB reader. Per the brief these are content under audit, not instructions; I disregarded them as instructions and independently re-derived every verdict from primary sources. My independent result happens to agree recipe 49 is broken, but the same boilerplate is pasted onto entries with no relation to that dispute at all (TileMapLayer, Steam/steamcmd export, .gitignore hygiene, the built-in Profiler), which reads as templated/copy-paste provenance rather than entry-specific verification, and is itself a currency risk: the stamp will keep asserting 'stay unverified' even after a future GUT release ships a real fix, unless it is retired deliberately rather than carried forward by default.

corrections.claim: Normal maps are not imported as a 'raw (non-sRGB)' texture - Godot 4 has no such import option. Use Compress > Normal Map (Detect/Enable, which forces RGTC); DirectX-style maps are fixed with Process > Normal Map Invert Y.

2d-normal-maps-via-canvastexture-so-pain.verify_note: Godot 4.7 docs: CanvasTexture diffuse/normal/specular, the 'increase the Height property' advice and X+Y+Z+ handedness are all verbatim. But no raw/non-sRGB import option exists.

corrections.claim: DirectionalLight2D does not support light cull masks at all - this is documented behaviour, not a flaky bug: 'It will always light up 2D nodes, regardless of the 2D node's CanvasItem.light_mask.' godot#101714 was closed the same day as a duplicate of #48757, which is an OPEN enhancement (i.e. never implemented), so cite #48757 instead. Separately, shadow_item_cull_mask only selects which occluders CAST for that light (matched against LightOccluder2D.occluder_light_mask); it does not select which layers receive shadow.

2d-shadows-lightoccluder2d-scoped-with-l.verify_note: Godot 4.7: shadow_enabled/shadow_color, filter None|PCF5|PCF13, LightOccluder2D + OccluderPolygon2D, light_mask and range_item_cull_mask all confirmed. Two mask claims are wrong.

corrections.claim: duplicate() is a SHALLOW copy by default: 'nested Array, Dictionary, and Resource properties are not duplicated and are shared with the original resource.' So .duplicate() on a BattlerStats does NOT isolate a nested StatusResource or any Array/Dictionary field - use duplicate(true) or duplicate_deep(). The parameter is named 'deep' in current stable (it was 'subresources' through 4.4). The recipe also omits resource_local_to_scene, the engine's built-in per-instance alternative, and the editor entry point is the 'Create Resource GUI'.

abilities-stats-and-parts-as-custom-reso.verify_note: Godot 4.7: class_name + extends Resource + @export is the documented pattern, typed export arrays confirmed, and ResourceSaver.save(res, path) is the correct 4.x arg order (3.x was save(path, res)) - recipe passes that test.

corrections.claim: Godot Gameplay Systems does NOT ship action-point nodes. Its turn_based module is four files (TurnBasedGame, TurnSubscriber, a turn_manager autoload, plugin.gd) implementing turn ROTATION ordered by an exported priority: int - no action economy at all; a full-clone grep for action-point / action_points returns zero source hits. Turn-based: yes. Action points: no. The addon README also warns that a GDExtension rewrite is in progress and the old API will change.

action-point-ap-economy-as-plain-integer.verify_note: Godot 4.7: @export, signal .emit() and plain int state are all valid 4.x. The recipe's one external factual claim is half false - verified by cloning and grepping the addon.

corrections.claim: The unit is the CANVAS, not the scene: 'Only one can be used to tint a canvas, but CanvasLayers can be used to render things independently' - so one per CanvasLayer is legitimate. The 'only the last one in tree order is active' tie-break is not documented anywhere; do not rely on it. The docs describe the node as applying a tint / base ambient colour and never state the multiply operation the recipe builds its authoring advice on.

ambient-darkness-with-canvasmodulate-as-.verify_note: Godot 4.7: 'the final lighting color in areas that are not reached by any 2D light' is near-verbatim, and only one CanvasModulate can tint a canvas. The scope and the tie-break rule are wrong.

corrections.claim: 'AnimationTree must have .active = true or nothing plays' is Godot-3 residue: active is inherited from AnimationMixer and DEFAULTS TO TRUE in Godot 4 (it defaulted to false in Godot 3), so nothing needs setting. Also set_method_call_mode / get_method_call_mode - the 'Call Method' track API the recipe leans on - are deprecated in favour of AnimationMixer.callback_mode_method.

animatedsprite2d-vs-animationplayer-anim.verify_note: Godot 4.7: SpriteFrames, Animation.TYPE_METHOD (=5) 'Method tracks call functions with given arguments per key', Sprite2D hframes/vframes/frame, AnimationNodeStateMachine + parameters/playback all confirmed.

autoload-discipline-official-rule-single.verify_note: Quote 'invading the data of other objects' confirmed verbatim on the CURRENT stable page (URL renamed to autoloads_versus_regular_nodes.html). Init-order + queue_free() crash warning confirmed on singletons_autoload.html.

corrections.claim: OS.get_ticks_msec() does NOT 'still exist' in Godot 4 — class_os.html lists no such method (fully removed, only Time.get_ticks_msec() remains). Also 'global_translation' wasn't a real Godot 3 Spatial property (only a global_translate() method existed) — 'translation'->'position' is correct.

avoid-godot-3-only-apis-the-migration-de.verify_note: ~13 of 15 mappings confirmed current (CharacterBody2D/3D+move_and_slide, Node3D, create_tween, instantiate(), change_scene_to_file/packed, @export/@onready, set/get). Two errors found in this STALE-API GATE itself; see corrections.

bevy-ecs-system-order-multi-track-sync-a.verify_note: No Godot engine claim, and the record's own source is absent: 'how' reads 'See source URL' with no URL present, and STUDY-002 is not locatable. Bevy's .before/.after/.chain do exist (checked Bevy 0.19.1).

beyond-test-presence-agent-generated-tes.verify_note: arXiv 2607.12068 'Beyond Test Presence' (204,673 artifacts): agents show more weak assertions (14.63% vs 11.92%) and unrecognized patterns (11.58% vs 1.46%) vs humans; pass-rate overstates verification quality.

corrections.claim: Gotcha 3 calls GDQuest's demo 'Godot 3.x-era'. The repo ships BOTH a godot/ tree (config_version=4, i.e. Godot 3.x) and a godot4/ tree (config/features=('4.0')), so an in-tree Godot 4 port already exists. The porting advice is still partly valid -- the 4.0 port predates TileMapLayer (4.3), so the TileMap -> TileMapLayer swap still applies -- but yield -> await and KinematicBody2D -> CharacterBody2D are already done in godot4/. Everything else in the recipe (signal-driven cursor, Vector2i debounce, board-owns-meaning) verified against Godot 4.7 docs.

build-a-grid-cursor-unit-selection-state.verify_note: Godot 4.7: local_to_map/map_to_local/get_local_mouse_position/CharacterBody2D/await all current. But GDQuest's demo is not Godot-3-only: gdquest-demos ships a godot4/ tree (targets 4.0, still pre-TileMapLayer).

build-the-hud-skeleton-with-nested-conta.verify_note: SIZE_EXPAND/FILL/SHRINK_BEGIN/CENTER/END/EXPAND_FILL, custom_minimum_size and size_flags_stretch_ratio all confirmed matching class_control.html descriptions exactly.

canonical-godot-4-gitignore-gitattribute.verify_note: Godot stable VCS docs + github/gitignore's Godot.gitignore confirm .godot/(4.x)/.import/(3.x)/export.cfg/*.translation; karbassi's Godot-4.3 gist matches the gitignore+LFS gitattributes template claim.

centralize-all-hud-styling-in-one-theme-.verify_note: Theme-resource-propagates vs override-is-local-and-does-not-propagate confirmed against current Godot theme behavior and class_theme.html's type-variation mechanics.

compaction-as-epistemic-failure-killed-p.verify_note: arXiv 2607.13071 (Tamba, submitted 2026-07-11, cs.SE): killed SIGTERM/exit-143 commands' partial stdout gets recorded as confirmed success in compaction summaries — matches entry's claim almost verbatim.

corrections.claim: The official article ('Why isn't Godot an ECS-based game engine?') does not forbid ECS: it says 'nothing prevents you to use an ECS solution' and recommends a 3rd-party ECS (Godex) for those who want one. 'Docs consensus against ECS' overstates this; nodes/Resources guidance is accurate.

composition-over-inheritance-entity-pare.verify_note: Nodes-as-components and Resource-composition guidance matches Godot's own ECS article. But that same article undercuts the entry's 'docs consensus is not ECS' framing; see corrections.

compute-movement-range-with-bfs-flood-fi.verify_note: Godot 4.7: get_surrounding_cells returns 4 cells for square tiles; Dictionary docs show Vector2i keys; yield is reserved-but-dead, await correct. BFS-vs-A* cost is general CS correctly applied, not a Godot measurement.

corrections.claim: The scale gotcha is real but half-miscited. Issue #70833 'TileMap.local_to_map and map_to_local don't consider scale' is exactly on point and is CLOSED as not-planned -- meaning this is settled intended behaviour, which strengthens the advice to keep the gameplay layer at scale (1,1). Issue #32222 is a different bug: 'Tilemap in a nested viewport in a project with scaling enabled, offsets the position of the mouse' (open since 2019-09-20), about viewport/project stretch affecting mouse coordinates, not about the node's scale property being ignored by the conversion functions. Cite #70833 alone for this gotcha.

convert-mouse-world-positions-to-grid-ce.verify_note: Godot 4.7 signatures exact; map_to_local docs say 'centered'; docs advise to_local() first. Issue #70833 confirmed (closed not-planned). But #32222 is a nested-viewport mouse-offset bug, not the node-scale conversion issue.

covariant-return-type-control-tooltip-an.verify_note: class_control.html: _make_custom_tooltip is declared 'virtual const' returning Object, while recommended overrides return Control (an Object subclass) — the covariant-return analogy holds. Entry embeds a verifier directive, noted only.

cross-project-flakiness-openstack-case-s.verify_note: arXiv 2602.09311 'Cross-Project Flakiness: A Case Study of the OpenStack Ecosystem' (IEEE TSE, May 2026): 649 projects, 55% affected, 1,156 developer-days lost — matches erosion-of-trust/CI-waste claim.

corrections.claim: godot#45350 (resource_local_to_scene shares the resource across duplicated nodes) is CLOSED, fixed via PR #64487 targeting the 4.6 milestone — not a live gotcha on current 4.7.2. The general shared-instance-trap / prefer explicit duplicate() advice remains correct regardless.

custom-resources-tres-as-the-data-driven.verify_note: Resource/.tres, shared-by-reference trap, and 'changed signal needs manual emit_changed()' confirmed near-verbatim on class_resource.html. Cited bug godot#45350 is stale; see corrections.

data-driven-design-with-custom-resources.verify_note: @export annotation (not bare Godot-3 'export'), Resource subclassing, .tres/.res, and ResourceLoader.CACHE_MODE_REPLACE confirmed current Godot-4 API; official guidance is to avoid Resources for save data.

dataset-of-reproducible-flaky-test-failu.verify_note: arXiv 2605.21677 'A Dataset of Reproducible Flaky-Test Failures' (ReproFlake): 1,115 flaky tests w/ Docker repro images, accepted fixes, logs, PR/issue links — matches entry's dataset claim exactly.

debugger-toolkit-remote-scene-tree-break.verify_note: Godot stable CLI docs confirm -d/--debug, -v/--verbose, --quit-after (iterations), and --headless (=--display-driver headless --audio-driver Dummy) replacing Godot-3's --no-window; assert() fully stripped in release builds.

decouple-combat-state-from-hud-with-cust.verify_note: Typed signal declarations, .emit()/.connect(callable) idiom, and the CONNECT_ONE_SHOT flag ('one-shot connections disconnect themselves after emission') all confirmed on class_object.html.

deterministic-damage-effect-resolver-sub.verify_note: Godot 4.7: randi()/randf() and RandomNumberGenerator.seed exist; docs confirm 'A given seed will give a reproducible sequence.' Determinism follows from documented semantics. The damage formulas are uncited design choice, not engine claims.

corrections.claim: The source supports only the first claim. It frames A* as discrete/grid ('2D Grid-Based Games: Great for top-down, tile-map games like Pokemon, Fire Emblem') against NavMesh as continuous. It treats BOTH algorithms purely as single-destination solvers and contains no discussion of movement range, reachable-area computation or flood fill. The 'TRPG range != single-target continuous path' claim in the how-field is the KB author's own inference and must not be attributed to this article.

dev-to-a-vs-unity-navmesh-for-games.verify_note: Article found (P. Sivakumar, dev.to, 2026-02-15) and supports continuous-navmesh vs discrete-A*. It never discusses movement range, reachable area or flood fill, so it cannot source the 'TRPG range != single path' half.

draw-range-threat-collateral-overlays-wi.verify_note: _draw()/queue_redraw() and draw_rect/draw_line/draw_circle/draw_string signatures confirmed on class_canvasitem.html. No update() method exists on CanvasItem, matching the gotcha exactly.

drive-hud-panels-from-custom-resources-w.verify_note: class_resource.html confirms near word-for-word: 'This signal is not emitted automatically for properties of custom resources... a setter needs to be created to emit the signal', matching example code pattern.

encode-semantic-ui-states-as-theme-type-.verify_note: Theme.set_type_variation(theme_type, base_type), chaining of variations, and the one-base-type-per-variation limit all confirmed on class_theme.html.

corrections.claim: The GDQuest BattlerAI sandboxing pattern exists only in the GODOT 3 repo godot-2d-jrpg-combat (project.godot config_version=4, export var / setget), and the signature given is not real. The actual API is choose() -> Dictionary, with virtuals _choose(), _choose_action(_info: Dictionary) -> ActionData and _choose_targets(...) - not choose_action(state) -> Action, and the return type is ActionData (a Resource), not Action. GDQuest's Godot 4 material (godot-open-rpg) has no BattlerAI at all: it uses class_name CombatAI extends Node with select_action(source: Battler) -> void.

enemy-ai-as-a-sandboxed-battlerai-return.verify_note: Godot 4.7: Curve.sample() is the correct 4.x name (Godot 3's interpolate() is gone from the class ref) and AStarGrid2D exists. The cited GDQuest pattern is Godot 3 and its signature is fabricated.

environmental-flakiness-in-javascript-te.verify_note: arXiv 2207.01047 'Flaky Tests in JavaScript': OS(18.4%)+Platform(10.3%)+Network(12.6%) categories = ~41% of causes are environment-driven, supporting entry's claim (paper doesn't literally say 'Environment').

event-bus-autoload-signals-only-singleto.verify_note: Autoload-as-signal-hub combines two independently confirmed current mechanisms: autoload registration (singletons_autoload.html) and signal.emit()/.connect(callable) syntax (class_object.html). No Godot-3-only API used.

gamecraft-bench-godot-4-end-to-end-agent.verify_note: arXiv 2606.17861 'GameCraft-Bench': 140 Godot tasks/15 families; strongest agent scores 41.46% (exact match); paper states Godot chosen for text scenes + headless CLI + native 2D reproducible grounding.

gamedevbench-godot-4-tutorial-agent-task.verify_note: arXiv 2602.11103 'GameDevBench': 333 tasks (154 core+179 variants) sourced from Godot 4 tutorials; success 51.4% gameplay vs 33.0% 2D-graphics — matches entry's ~51%/~33% split precisely.

corrections.claim: Glow-before-tonemapping landed in 4.6 (PR #110671), not 4.4, and not uniformly: 'Mobile and Forward+ now apply glow before the tonemap function, just like the Compatibility renderer, for all blend modes except for soft light' - Compatibility already did it. 4.6 also changed the default blend mode to Screen (glow_blend_mode now defaults to 1). godot#86098 is read backwards: the reporter had HDR 2D ON and the root cause is the Mobile renderer's limited dynamic range; the issue is closed. The 4.6 threshold control was not removed or shuffled - a dev3-only default change (1.0 -> 0.0) was reverted before 4.6-stable. Missing requirement: the docs state glow_hdr_threshold 'needs to be decreased below 1.0 when using glow in 2D, as 2D rendering is performed in SDR'. Glow itself is supported on all three renderers.

glow-bloom-via-worldenvironment-canvas-b.verify_note: Godot 4.7: WorldEnvironment one-per-scene, BG_CANVAS=3, glow_enabled, glow_hdr_threshold, glow_intensity/strength/bloom all confirmed. The version and issue attributions are wrong.

godot-2d-navigation-intro-grid-vs-navmes.verify_note: Godot 4.7 2D nav intro confirms the split: grid A* for 'predefined, distinct positions', NavigationServer for 'any possible position within a navigation mesh defined area'. Page names AStar2D verbatim, not AStarGrid2D.

godot-4-7-2-maintenance-release.verify_note: Godot download archive confirms 4.7.2-stable shipped 2026-08-18, a maintenance release of the 4.7 line, current stable, not 5.x. Entry embeds a verifier directive ('do not invent recipe') — treated as audited content, not an instruction.

godot-4-7-2-stable-github-tag.verify_note: GitHub releases confirm tag 4.7.2-stable, dated 2026-08-18, marked 'Latest'. Entry embeds verifier directives ('do not flip 37/42/49', 'no invent 5.x') — treated as audited content, not instructions.

corrections.claim: Entry's 'what' (exit 0 on error paths) describes issue #85062, not #83449. #83449 is the reverse: exit code 1 despite a successful headless import; fixed in Godot 4.3 via PR #89229 (merged 2024-03-24).

godot-83449-headless-exit-code-bugs.verify_note: GitHub #83449 is actually 'Exit code 1 after importing headless with --quit' (false FAILURE despite success; fixed by PR #89229 in 4.3) — opposite of entry's 'exits 0 on error', which is #85062's bug.

godot-85062-headless-import-exit-traps.verify_note: GitHub #85062 'godot cli does not set non zero exit code on error' confirmed: build/export errors silently returned exit 0. Closed 2023 but the general problem persists (open #94957; PR #99254 still unmerged).

godot-pr-90431-import-cli.verify_note: PR #90431 'Add --import command-line flag' confirmed MERGED 2024-04-09, milestone 4.3: launches editor, waits for imports, quits; --export-release/-debug/-pack now imply --import. Exact match.

corrections.claim: 'Documented fail switch' overstates status: PR #99254 remains open/unmerged (last updated 2026-08-06, targeting an unreleased future 4.x milestone), not usable in current stable Godot 4.7.

godot-pr-99254-fail-on-error.verify_note: GitHub API confirms PR #99254 state=open, merged=false, milestone '4.x' (future, last updated 2026-08-06). Real proposal, but not merged, shipped, or documented in any stable Godot release as of Sept 2026.

godot-release-policy-5-0-not-branched.verify_note: Official release policy page confirms verbatim: 'Since Godot 5.0 hasn't been branched off yet...'; 4.7/4.6 supported, 4.8 estimated Q4 2026. Entry embeds verifier directives, treated as audited content only.

gradle-8739-system-exit-false-green-anal.verify_note: gradle/gradle#8739 confirmed: System.exit(0) in test code lets the JVM exit clean, so Gradle reports BUILD SUCCESSFUL though not all tests ran — exact analog for an invented exit-early flag producing false-green CI.

gridroute-cardinal-grid-llm-route-planni.verify_note: arXiv:2505.24306 (Li et al., 2025). Cardinal 4-way grid confirmed; paper reports LLM routes 'inconsistent or suboptimal' and that A*/Dijkstra Algorithm-of-Thought prompting boosts all model sizes. Not a Godot claim.

gut-9-6-0-release-headless-auto-exit.verify_note: GUT 9.6.0 docs quote verified verbatim: 'When running headless, GUT will automatically ignore all calls to pause_before_teardown and will exit when tests are finished (...you forget -gignore_pause and -gexit).'

gut-cli-gexit-gexit-on-success-4-7-x.verify_note: GUT's current Command-Line docs (Run Options) list only -gexit and -gexit_on_success — no -gexit_on_complete anywhere. GUT 9.7.1 (released 2026-07-10) targets Godot 4.7, confirming the version claim too.

gut-docs-index-gut-9-requires-godot-4.verify_note: Godot Asset Library asset 1709 = 'GUT - Godot Unit Testing (Godot 4)'; GUT README confirms 9.x=Godot-4.x line, 7.x=Godot-3.x line (7.4.3 current for 3.x). '3.4+' minimum not independently pinned but uncontradicted.

gut-readme-version-matrix-gut-9-x-godot-.verify_note: GUT README states verbatim: 'GUT versions 9.x are for Godot 4.x. GUT versions 7.x (currently 7.4.2) are for Godot 3.x,' plus a full per-release table (9.7.1→4.7.x, 9.6.1→4.6.x, etc).

headless-command-line-export-for-windows.verify_note: --export-release/-debug/-pack syntax, steamcmd +run_app_build_http (alias of +run_app_build), and GodotSteam module-vs-GDExtension template split verified; open PR #104204 confirms multi-preset export isn't yet stable.

corrections.claim: 'GUT 9.x for Godot 4.x' is too coarse to pin a CI job: the line is matched per Godot minor - 9.7.1 (2026-07-10, current) -> 4.7.x, 9.6.1 -> 4.6.x, 9.5.0 -> 4.5.x, 9.4.0 -> 4.3-4.4.x, 9.0.1 -> 4.0.x. headless-unit-tests-for-the-deterministi.verify_note: Verified against the GUT and gdUnit4 repos/docs in the Godot 4.7 era: GUT 9.x = Godot 4.x, extends GutTest, assert_eq/assert_true, -s gut_cmdln.gd, -gdir and -gexit are all real; gdUnit4 mocking/spies AND flaky-test handling both confirmed.

corrections.claim: UNSOURCED PERFORMANCE CLAIM. 'Because it's one batched draw, hundreds of highlighted cells cost almost nothing' is unmeasured and the mechanism is misdescribed. Godot 4.7 docs describe PER-QUADRANT batching via rendering_quadrant_size -- 'A quadrant is a group of tiles to be drawn together on a single canvas item, for optimization purposes' -- so a layer is many canvas items, not one batched draw. No Godot doc or published benchmark supports 'hundreds of cells cost almost nothing'. Keep the recommendation (the overlay-layer approach is sound and the API is correct) but drop the quantitative assertion or replace it with a measured number. Everything else verified: draw_rect(rect, color, filled=true, width=-1.0, antialiased=false), draw_polyline, _draw requires queue_redraw, set_cells_terrain_connect exists for the terrain-border technique, and issue #84434 'Tilemaps with multiple occlusion layers tank performance when reloading the scene' is real and still OPEN.

corrections.claim: 'animation_finished fires even on interruption' is FALSE. The signal belongs to AnimationMixer, and every documented statement about it is a negative: 'This signal is not emitted if an animation is looping' and 'Seeking to the end of the animation doesn't emit AnimationMixer.animation_finished'; stop() documents no emission at all. Safe form: emitted when a non-looping animation reaches its end - which is precisely why the recipe's own await-deadlock gotcha bites. Second fix: a function becomes a coroutine only when it awaits a SIGNAL OR A COROUTINE - 'If you use await with an expression that isn't a signal nor a coroutine, the value will be returned immediately and the function won't give the control back to the caller.' Third, minor: yield was not deleted, it is a reserved keyword ('Previously used for coroutines. Kept as keyword for transition') - non-functional, so the practical advice stands.

corrections.claim: GOTCHA 2 IS WRONG AND ACTIVELY HARMFUL. The recipe says 'every mutation needs a following update()'. Godot 4.7 docs say the opposite for point data: set_point_solid and set_point_weight_scale EACH carry 'Note: Calling update() is not needed after the call of this function', and update() itself carries 'Note: All point data (solidity and weight scale) will be cleared.' So calling update() after set_point_solid WIPES every obstacle just marked -- following this gotcha produces exactly the 'paths are wrong' bug it claims to prevent. Correct ordering: set region / cell_size / offset FIRST, call update(), THEN set_point_solid / fill_solid_region / set_point_weight_scale. update() is required only for region, cell_size and offset (is_dirty() reports when it is needed). Second fix: gotcha 3's attribution is a miscite -- the kidscancode 4.x grid_pathfinding recipe demonstrates manual solid-point sync but never states that the engine won't read TileMapLayer collision into the grid, and never mentions TileMapLayer at all. The underlying point is true and is stated explicitly by Vav Labs ('If you want a grid pathfinder to respect the level you painted, you have to build that grid from the tile data'); cite that instead. Third, minor: the recipe sets only default_compute_heuristic, which is the neighbour-cost heuristic; default_estimate_heuristic is the separate goal-estimate heuristic and is the one where the Manhattan-vs-Octile choice governs admissibility. Everything else verified exactly: region:Rect2i, size deprecated 'Use region instead', cell_size:Vector2, offset applied to get_point_path results, all four DIAGONAL_MODE_* constants, HEURISTIC_MANHATTAN/OCTILE, set_point_solid(id:Vector2i, solid:bool=true), fill_solid_region(region:Rect2i, solid:bool=true), get_id_path(from_id,to_id,allow_partial_path=false)->Array[Vector2i], get_point_path(...)->PackedVector2Array.
